sections.overview: The White-tailed Ptarmigan is a small grouse of alpine tundra in western North America.
sections.identification: Its plumage turns brown in summer and white in winter; the tail, wings and feathered feet remain white.
sections.habitat: It lives above the treeline in western mountains and remains at high elevations throughout its life cycle.
sections.diet: Its plant-rich diet includes willow buds and twigs, leaves, flowers, berries and lichens; chicks also take insects.
sections.behavior: In winter it often avoids flight and shelters in snowbanks, conserving energy in its exposed mountain habitat.
sections.reproduction: Females make ground nests and usually lay four to seven eggs; incubation lasts about three weeks.
sections.ecology: In parts of the Yukon it shares alpine habitat with the larger Rock Ptarmigan, Lagopus muta.
sections.conservation: Cornell lists the species as low concern, while noting that unusually warm weather can stress these cold-adapted birds.
